1                     UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                       
2                          DISTRICT OF NEVADA                            
3                                  * * *                                 

4   CIRILO UCHARIMA ALVARADO,           Case No. 3:22-CV-00249-MMD-CLB   

5                             Plaintiff,  ORDER GRANTING MOTION TO STAY  
                                                 DISCOVERY               
6        v.                                                              
                                                [ECF No. 261]            
7   WESTERN RANGE ASSOCIATION, et                                        
    al.,                                                                 
8                                                                        
                           Defendants.                                   
9                                                                        
         Currently pending before the Court is Defendants Western Range Association 
10                                                                        
    (“WRA”), Ellison Ranching Company, John Espil Sheep Co., Inc., F.I.M. Corp., The Little 
11                                                                        
    Paris Sheep Company, LLC, Borda Land & Sheep Company, Holland Ranch LLC, Need 
12                                                                        
    More Sheep Co., LLC, and Faulkner Land and Livestock Company, Inc.’s (collectively the 
13                                                                        
    “Ranch Defendants”, and together with WRA, “Defendants”) joint motion to stay discovery 
14                                                                        
    pending the District Court’s determination of pending motions to dismiss. (ECF No. 261.) 
15                                                                        
    Plaintiff Cirilo Ucharima Alvarado (“Plaintiff”) responded, (ECF No. 270), and Defendants 
16                                                                        
    replied, (ECF No. 272). The Court has reviewed the relevant pleadings and papers, and, 
17                                                                        
    for the reasons set for below, grants Defendants’ motion to stay discovery. 
18                                                                        
         To determine if a stay is appropriate pending the ruling on a motion to dismiss, a 
19                                                                        
    court must consider the following factors: (1) whether the pending motion is potentially 
20                                                                        
    dispositive  of  the  case;  (2)  whether  the  motion  can  be  decided  without  additional 
21                                                                        
    discovery; and (3) whether the court is convinced that the plaintiff cannot state a claim for 
22                                                                        
    relief. Kor Media Group, LLC v. Green, 294 F.R.D. 579, 581 (D. Nev. 2013).1 The Court 
23                                                                        
    must take a “preliminary peek” at the merits of the underlying dispositive motion in order 
24                                                                        
    to find whether the plaintiff can state a claim. Tradebay, LLC v. eBay, Inc., 278 F.R.D. 
25                                                                        

26                                                                        
    1    The  undersigned  follows  the  majority  approach  within  the  District  when 
    adjudicating motions to stay discovery—i.e., the preliminary peek framework outlined in 
27                                                                        
    Kor Media—and expressly adopts the analysis from Judge Koppe’s recent order in Flynn 
    v. Nevada, 345 F.R.D. 338 (D. Nev. 2024), which rejects the minority “good cause” 
1|    597, 603 (D.  Nev. 2011). The “preliminary peek” does not prejudge the outcome of the 
2 |  motion; it merely evaluates whether an order staying discovery is warranted. /d. 
3          In conducting its review, the Court also considers the goal of Federal Rule of Civil 
4    Procedure  1,  which  provides  that the  Rules  should  “be  construed,  administered,  and 
5 |  employed  by  the  court  and  the  parties  to  secure  the just,  speedy,  and  inexpensive 
6 |  determination of every action.” Fed.  R. Civ.  P.  1. With  Rule 1  as its prime directive, the 
7 |  court must decide whether it is more just to speed the parties along in discovery while a 
     dispositive  motion  is  pending  or  to  delay  discovery  to  accomplish  the  inexpensive 
     determination of the case.  See Big City Dynasty v. FP Holdings, L.P.,  336 F.R.D. 507, 
      512 (D. Nev. 2020). 
11          Having reviewed all the factors set forth above and after conducting a “preliminary 
     peek” of the underlying motions, the Court finds that a stay of discovery pending resolution 
13    of the motions to dismiss, is appropriate in this case. Accordingly, Defendants’ motion to 
     stay discovery,  (ECF No. 261),  is GRANTED.  In the event resolution of the motions to 
     dismiss do not result in  dismissal, the parties shall submit an amended joint proposed 
16 |  discovery plan within 14 days of resolution of the motions. 
17          IT IS SO ORDERED. 
18          DATED:  February 28, 2025                                . 
19 
20                                        UNITED STATES\MAGISTRATE JUDGE
